note: Gmail content goes to the claude/codex CLI on a consumer subscription where training on input is on by default: a violation of Google Limited Use item 4 (legal blocker).

gmail logout kept synced Gmail data: shipped a separate explicit 'delete synced Gmail data' action (CLI plus button) with logout unchanged, and removeGoogleAccount calls ClearGmailData before DeleteGoogleAccount.
The Workspace policy requires user help documentation explaining how users manage and delete their data; the CLI command exists, the documentation does not (not code).
The memory alias gmailthread:<thread_id> is not account-scoped, so two mailboxes sharing a thread id would merge their episodes.
GetGmailBodyByID selected WHERE id = ? with no account_id: renamed to GetGmailBody(accountID, id) and scoped, the account read from the item's channel_id by GmailAccountIDFromChannelID.
The memory vault is a git repo: eviction writes a tombstone and the content remains in history; the vault is not declared in the privacy policy.
No URL-scheme allowlist: the text of a Slack message became a clickable link of any scheme (smb://, file://) while the sandbox is disabled.
Three OAuth client secrets (Slack/Google/Jira) can be extracted from the binary with strings.
install.sh: checksum was fail-open, signatures were not verified, quarantine was removed, files were copied with sudo.
No PKCE in the Google OAuth flow (even though it was implemented for Outlook).
Deleting a source does not cascade into derived data (memory, people cards); upstream deletions are not handled.
Untrusted content lands in the system prompt rather than the user message at 11 call sites; the Workspace policy lists prompt injection protection as a checklist item.
MemoryView deliberately handed every non-watchtower-memory URL scheme to the system.
track_events.source_refs from LLM output went to Link(destination:) with no validation.
curl | sh from the main branch of a third-party repo in CI.
review-rules.md proposed responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim as the TCC fix; it was tried and rolled back (it changed the responsibility chain but not the subject in the TCC prompt).

Refresh tokens and IMAP passwords in 0600 files instead of Keychain: withdrawn 2026-08-03 as a deliberate decision (gcloud precedent, no normative requirement, Keychain hostile to the headless daemon and CLI).
Qwen3 weights come from a personal Hugging Face account with no revision pinning.
Fail-open GrantsScope: an empty scope in the token response meant granted.
Unclear how codex parses -c developer_instructions=<value>; if parsed as a TOML document, string injection could disable the sandbox.
The vault was written 0644/0755 and watchtower.db 0644; both now 0600/0700, tightened on open so pre-existing installs are brought up too.
.env is still 0644 - a file on the developer's machine, not in the repo: fix with chmod 600 .env.
Content in logs: the full target text without truncation, and 200 characters of model output in pipeline_runs.error_msg.
A stale system prompt pushed the agent toward a sqlite3 shell fallback (Bash is available on codex).
Prompt injection to arbitrary command execution: the AI chat was granted an unsandboxed Bash(sqlite3*), whose dot-commands (.shell, .system, .load) run OS commands from Slack/Jira text.
The AI chat got full read/write SQLite access through the reference mcp-server-sqlite (mcp__sqlite__* includes write_query), bypassing Watchtower's read-only MCP contract.
Slack OAuth login installed a 10-year CA certificate (IsCA, KeyUsageCertSign, no name constraints) as a trusted SSL root with its private key on disk.
Auto-update signature verification accepted ad-hoc signatures (no Team ID or designated requirement) and then stripped quarantine.
AI-generated source_refs were rendered as clickable links with a hidden destination and no URL-scheme validation.
Markdown rendering in the AI chat created clickable links with any URL scheme taken from the model's output; no OpenURLAction restricted schemes.
The Slack user token (and Google/Jira OAuth tokens) are stored as plaintext 0600 files, never in Keychain; same decision as S-3.
.gitignore ignores only the exact name watchtower, so a stray watchtower-new binary (which may embed OAuth client secrets via ldflags) could be committed by git add .
